research_question: Under matched update tokens and compute, does framework-curated recent Python change data improve executable coding utility over raw-random and Stage-A-random data while preserving prior capabilities?

primary.selection_reason: Exact 4B base model with coding capability; post-release data gives a defensible temporal non-exposure boundary.

transfer_replication.selection_reason: Code-specific base model with documented The Stack v2 provenance and opt-out handling.

claim_scope.primary: parameter-efficient continued pretraining on recently collected Python change bundles

collection_contract.source_type: public merged pull requests and associated repository state
collection_contract.training_payload_rule: Repository code, tests, and documentation may enter training only when covered by an allowlisted repository license and after content, provenance, split, and contamination gates pass. Issue and pull-request prose is retained for provenance and executable evaluation but excluded from training unless a separate documented use basis is recorded.
collection_contract.execution_validation_boundary: Verified executable test commands are required for executable-evaluation eligibility, not for licensed training-content eligibility. Execution failures remain Stage-C/evaluation blockers and must not silently approve an executable task.
acquisition_rules: use approved public APIs or reproducible public archives
honor source rate limits, access controls, deletion signals, and opt-out requirements
record acquisition timestamp, source URL, commit identity, and collector version
do not bypass authentication, access restrictions, or robots and policy controls
repository_requirements: test suite or executable validation command exists
merge commit and parent commit are reproducibly fetchable
repository is not assigned to another split
hard_exclusions: generated, vendored, minified, binary, lock, or dependency snapshot files
secrets, credentials, or detected high-risk PII
exact or hard near-duplicate of an evaluation item

split_contract.repository_assignment_algorithm: sha256(normalized_repository_identity) modulo 100; train buckets 0-79, development 80-89, confirmatory 90-99
split_contract.same_repository_temporal_holdout: secondary diagnostic only; never primary confirmation

never_training_sources: SWE-bench and Multi-SWE-bench task repositories and patches
checks: exact normalized text and code hashes
problem statement and test signature search

stage_b: repository, API, change-type, and difficulty coverage support
release_layer: select release construction under a frozen deployment contract
add frozen general replay if required by retention evidence

budget.purpose: retain a disjoint Stage-A pool large enough for later equal-budget counterfactual construction

coverage_support.role: selection constraint only; never part of the ranking objective

stage_b_contract.claim_boundary: Stage-B Core-proxy engineering smoke only; no Utility, Stage-C, or training-release claim.

validation_philosophy.primary_stage_b_validation: automated metamorphic properties, frozen ablations, and equal-budget downstream Stage-C comparison
validation_philosophy.human_or_llm_review: optional diagnostic only; never selector ground truth, promotion gate, tuning signal, or Stage-C entry blocker
validation_philosophy.parameter_claim: frozen project hypotheses requiring ablation and untouched confirmatory evidence; not validated by citation alone

training_contract.full_parameter_replication: required before extending the claim beyond parameter-efficient continued pretraining

decoding.max_generation_tokens: frozen per benchmark before development comparison

future_release_rule.primary_effect: curated release must beat recipe-matched Stage-A random on the primary executable aggregate
future_release_rule.primary_confidence: one-sided 95% paired seed-level confidence bound must exceed zero
future_release_rule.practical_margin: freeze from the smoke calibration before development candidate selection; never derive it from confirmatory results
future_release_rule.holdout_robustness: must pass both repository-disjoint development and untouched confirmatory holdouts
future_release_rule.retention: must satisfy every frozen code and general retention non-inferiority guardrail

forbidden_uses: using Utility or benchmark outcomes in the Stage-B selector objective
changing collection or split rules after confirmatory results
training on benchmark tasks, solutions, repositories, or near-duplicates
claiming full-parameter update effectiveness from QLoRA results
claiming universal code curation effectiveness from Python-only evidence
assuming a repository code license automatically licenses issue or pull-request prose for training
utility_scope: Stage C validation only; never selector objective
claim_boundary: The protocol was preregistered before collection. Bounded collection and Stage-0/A/B engineering smokes now exist, but no Stage-C or 4B result has yet been produced.
